channel.title: Lapland.blog · Field journal from Finnish Lapland
channel.description: A first-person field journal from Finnish Lapland: honest, seasonal, written by someone who actually lives here. Aurora, cabins, seasons, food, people.

item.title: Seven and a half minutes a day
item.description: Nobody announces the end of the summer light. It just goes, at seven and a half minutes a day in Rovaniemi and nine in Utsjoki, until one evening in late August you cannot see the path to the woodshed.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: 154 Lapland rest areas lose their firewood service
item.description: Metsähallitus is ending firewood and toilet servicing at 154 rest areas. What it means for hikers, which Lapland sites are listed, and why the saving misses.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: July packing list for Lapland: what you actually need
item.description: The same July day can be a heatwave in the afternoon and windy and cold on the fell at night. How to pack ten days into one bag without carrying dead weight.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Lapland lake sauna: how to heat a wood-fired stove
item.description: A wood-fired sauna takes two hours to heat: time enough for the firewood, the whisk and the jetty. How a cabin guest runs a Lapland lake sauna, step by step.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Rovaniemi market in summer: strawberries, potatoes, vendace
item.description: Finnish strawberries reach the Rovaniemi market in early July. How the market works: when to go, what to buy, and how new potatoes and fried vendace are eaten.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Night hiking at Kiilopää: in July you start at midnight
item.description: In July the smartest time to hike the Kiilopää fells is at night: low golden light, cool air, and the mosquitoes stay in the birch. How a night hike works.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Sodankylä's midnight sun: when it shines and how to sleep
item.description: In Sodankylä the sun stays above the horizon from late May to mid-July. Here's how the light behaves, when it's at its best, and how to actually sleep.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Polar night in Rovaniemi: what the dark is and what helps
item.description: In Rovaniemi the polar night isn't total darkness but weeks of blue twilight. What it does to your body, and four habits that carry you to February.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Salmon soup in Rovaniemi: where to get it and what it costs
item.description: Three Rovaniemi restaurants serve salmon soup at 12–19 euros; several well-known places don't have it. Prices read from the menus on 14 September 2026.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Winter cabin week: what to pack for a Lapland forest cabin
item.description: Wood stove, a well and no signal: a week in a winter cabin near Kemijärvi works when the bag holds the right things. What you need, and what you'll forget.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Your aurora app can't see clouds: how to read the forecast
item.description: An aurora app alerts you about the Kp number, but clouds and town lights decide whether you see anything. Use the forecast once a day, then go outside.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Northern lights in Kemi: where to watch and what Kp means
item.description: Kemi lies south of the Arctic Circle, so the aurora needs a stronger night there than in Inari. How to read the forecast, choose a spot and survive the cold.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)
